title: Bug: test_add_rack failure due to unmatched Ethernet136 status
author: wenjwang-nv
body:
### Is it platform specific

mellanox

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

This ticket is used to track fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/24658

The configlet.test_add_rack.test_add_rack test has been flaky on Cisco-8102-C64 and Mellanox SN4600C/SN4700 platforms, while consistently passing on Arista. The failure manifests as PORT|Ethernet136 retaining admin_status: up in CONFIG_DB and APP_DB after the T0 removal patch, causing the DB comparison to fail across all 8 retry cycles.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run test_add_rack on specific platforms

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

AssertionError: DB compare failed after adding T0 via generic patch updater

### Relevant log output

```shell
duthost = , skip_load = True, hack_apply = False

    def generic_patch_rm_t0(duthost, skip_load=False, hack_apply=False):
        # Load config with T0
        #
        if not skip_load:
            duthost.copy(src=os.path.join(orig_db_dir, "config_db.json"),
                         dest="/etc/sonic/config_db.json")
            config_reload(duthost, wait=RELOAD_WAIT_TIME, start_bgp=True)
    
        if hack_apply:
            # Hack: TODO: Before removing port, patch updater need to ensure
            # the port is down. Until then bring it down explicitly.
            #
            for link in tor_data["links"]:
                tor_ifname = link["local"]["sonic_name"]
                duthost.shell("config interface shutdown {}".format(tor_ifname))
                do_pause(PAUSE_INTF_DOWN, "pause upon i/f {} shutdown before add patch".format(tor_ifname))
    
        patch_files = _list_patch_files(patch_rm_t0_dir)
    
        CMD = CMD_APPLY_HACK if hack_apply else CMD_APPLY
    
        for fl in patch_files:
            sonic_fl = os.path.join("/etc/sonic", fl)
            duthost.copy(src=os.path.join(patch_rm_t0_dir, fl), dest=sonic_fl)
            duthost.shell(CMD.format(sonic_fl), module_ignore_errors=True)
    
            # HACK: TODO: There are scenarios, where it applies patch and still consider as failed
            # "...Error: After applying patch to config, there are still some parts not updated\n"
            # The above error is possible, if some control plane component is making an update.
            # We can ignore rc, as DB comp is the final check. So skip it.
            # assert res["rc"] == 0, "Failed to apply patch"
    
        # Manual shutdown needed because the removal of admin_status won't operate shutdown. It will
        # by default keep the previous admin_status state. Thus making app-db comparison fail.
        for link in tor_data["links"]:
            tor_ifname = link["local"]["sonic_name"]
            duthost.shell("config interface shutdown {}".format(tor_ifname))
            do_pause(PAUSE_INTF_DOWN, "pause upon i/f {} shutdown before add patch".format(tor_ifname))
    
>       assert wait_until(DB_COMP_WAIT_TIME, 20, 0, db_comp, duthost, patch_rm_t0_dir,
                          no_t0_db_dir, "generic_patch_rm_t0"), \
            "DB compare failed after adding T0 via generic patch updater"
E       AssertionError: DB compare failed after adding T0 via generic patch updater
```

comments.author: StormLiangMS
comments.body:
Updated triage from 202605 nightly data:

- 108 deduplicated plan/testbed failures share the same `generic_patch_rm_t0` DB-compare assertion.
- The signature reproduces across Cisco-8102/8101, Arista-7260CX3, Mellanox-SN4600C, and Mellanox-SN4700, so it is not Mellanox-specific.
- Full logs show the generated no-T0 reference expects the selected physical interface `admin_status=up`, but the test unconditionally runs `config interface shutdown` after applying the remove patch.
- CONFIG_DB then differs on the PORT admin state; APP_DB keeps the LAG/member down and does not restore the expected route and neighbor entries.
- This also explains why PR #24658's forced-down target is not sufficient for the current failures; its exact `test_add_rack` CI failed.

Draft fix: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/26695

The fix restores each interface to the state captured in the generated no-T0 reference (`up`, or `down` when explicitly/default configured) before the existing DB comparison.

linkedPullRequests.title: [configlet]: Restore interface state after T0 removal
linkedPullRequests.author: StormLiangMS
linkedPullRequests.body:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Restore removed-rack interfaces to the admin state captured in the generated no-T0 reference configuration before comparing databases. The previous unconditional shutdown left interfaces down even when the reference expected them up, causing persistent CONFIG_DB and APP_DB mismatches across Cisco, Arista, and Mellanox 202605 testbeds.

Fixes #26098

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement


### Back port request

- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [x] 202605

Tracking issue/work item for backport/cherry-pick request (GitHub issue or Microsoft ADO): https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/26098
Failure type: day-one issue on 202605

### Tested branch

- [ ] master
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [x] 202605
- [ ] N/A

### Test result

- master: all PR checks passed, including `impacted-area-kvmtest-t1-lag` and `impacted-area-kvmtest-multi-asic-t1`.
- 202605: SONiC.20260510.08 - `configlet/test_add_rack.py` passed on the first attempt on all representative platforms:
  - Cisco-8102-C64: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a6b41d0101ed2146e809781
  - Arista-7260CX3-C64: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a6b41e1101ed2146e809784
  - Mellanox-SN4600C-C64: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a6b41f7c738d690ad9c1bbf

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?

In 202605 nightly results, the remove-T0 phase of `configlet/test_add_rack.py` repeatedly fails after the generated patch is applied. The no-T0 reference CONFIG_DB expects the selected physical interface to be up, while `generic_patch_rm_t0()` unconditionally shuts it down. The resulting state mismatch keeps the LAG member down and prevents the expected APP_DB routes and neighbors from returning.

The same failure signature was observed across Cisco-8000, Broadcom, and Mellanox platforms. PR #24658 forces the target state down, but that contradicts the current generated no-T0 reference state and its exact `test_add_rack` CI did not pass.

#### How did you do it?

Read the target interface state from `no_t0_db_dir/config_db.json` after applying the remove patch, then explicitly start or shut down each removed-rack interface to match that reference. If `admin_status` is omitted, preserve SONiC's default-down behavior. Also correct the remove-path assertion message.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Ran the repository pre-commit checks for the changed file, Python syntax validation, and a focused behavior check covering target `admin_status=up` and omitted/default-down states. The full PR pipeline passed, including both targeted T1 KVM jobs. Physical 202605 validation passed on Cisco-8102-C64, Arista-7260CX3-C64, and Mellanox-SN4600C-C64.

#### Any platform specific information?

The failure is not platform-specific. It has reproduced on Cisco-8102/8101, Arista-7260CX3, Mellanox-SN4600C, and Mellanox-SN4700.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A

### Documentation

N/A

comments.author: lipxu
comments.body:
**Verdict:** Solid, well-targeted bug fix — approving. It replaces the unconditional shutdown in `generic_patch_rm_t0()` with `_restore_interface_admin_status()`, which drives each interface's state from the no-T0 reference `config_db.json` instead of forcing it down. That's the correct root-cause fix for the CONFIG_DB/APP_DB mismatch in #26098, and the default-down handling plus the assertion-message correction are nice touches.

Two minor, optional suggestions:
1. Consider passing `tor_data` (or the links list) into `_restore_interface_admin_status` as a parameter instead of using the module global — cleaner and easier to unit-test.
2. Worth confirming the no-T0 reference always keeps PORT entries for these links; otherwise `assert isinstance(port_config, dict)` trips for every interface.
